article_title: Quiz-based inquiry: embedding incrementally sequenced questions to enhance engagement and learning in synchronous online lectures
citation: Zamzami Zainuddin, Michael Sailer, Shurui Bai, Madziatul Churiyah, Agung Winarno. (2026). Quiz-based inquiry: embedding incrementally sequenced questions to enhance engagement and learning in synchronous online lectures. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10614-1
title: Quiz-Based Inquiry (QBI) framework integrating Gagné's instructional events with inquiry-based learning phases
description: QBI is an instructional architecture in which formative assessment is the organising mechanism of synchronous online lectures. It uses "Gagné's events as scaffolds to organise inquiry throughout lectures, ensuring instructional structure provides coherence while inquiry processes add epistemic depth". Each lecture cycle runs question, response, peer comparison, instructor feedback, and conceptual consolidation, so questioning acts as a temporal scaffold regulating attention, dialogue, and conceptual development. The framework claims instruction and inquiry are not mutually exclusive.
requirements: Quiz prompts must be distributed across content segments and aligned with key conceptual shifts rather than administered as a single end-of-session block
Feedback must be immediate and integrated within the instructional cycle to support real-time adaptation
constraints: The article states IBL frameworks often give limited guidance on the timing of inquiry phases within lecture-based instruction, which QBI addresses
Effects were demonstrated in one course with three intact sections; the article notes possible novelty effects
target_learners: undergraduate students in synchronous online lectures
examples: The study operationalised QBI in 150-min sessions across three phases: orientation and cognitive activation, guided inquiry and collaborative exploration, and consolidation and formative evaluation

title: Dual-quiz architecture: discussion-oriented prompts during instruction plus evaluative prompts at transition points
description: This lesson-level pattern distributes two kinds of quiz prompts across a lecture session. As the article states, "A defining characteristic of QBI is its dual-quiz architecture: discussion-oriented prompts regulate inquiry during instruction, whereas evaluative prompts consolidate learning at key transition points". Discussion prompts trigger individual response, aggregated display, peer discussion, and instructor clarification; evaluative prompts emphasise retrieval, transfer, and application with immediate feedback. Together they integrate participation, feedback, and assessment into a recursive cycle.
requirements: Both prompt types must be distributed throughout the session rather than confined to the end
Real-time response visibility and structured peer discussion must follow responses
constraints: Designed for synchronous online lecture settings of about 150 minutes
Requires an interactive presentation platform or equivalent real-time response mechanism
examples: Sessions were organised into three phases: orientation and cognitive activation (30 minutes), guided inquiry and collaborative exploration (80 minutes), and consolidation and formative evaluation (40 minutes)
